children: Processor and AI accelerator designer AMD

received a higher price target from Susquehanna as shares traded at $515.185, up approximately 1.42%, at 10:20 a.m. ET. According to AD HOC News, analyst Christopher Rolland raised his target to $620 from $550a 12.7% increase. That gives investors a bigger number to chase. It also raises the bar for execution.

AMD's second-quarter results put revenue at $11.536 billion, including $6.7 billion from Data Center. That business grew 107% year over year and supplied roughly 58% of total sales. AI infrastructure is driving the revenue mix. Profitability still deserves scrutiny: AMD reported a 17% GAAP operating margin versus a 27% adjusted margin.

The valuation picture adds tension: shares sit 75.09% above the $294.24 GF Value estimate, suggesting a substantial premium under that model. Susquehanna's higher target signals optimism, but AMD still has to earn it. The next test is whether rising Data Center sales bring stronger margins and cash generation. Revenue growth carries more weight when the cash follows.

title: AMD Stocks Gain as $620 Target Raises the Execution Bar
